causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Cool morning temperatures of around 9°C drove high demand

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Wind and solar output, which is generally low-priced, was low due to calm and cloudy weather conditions.

causes.label: solar_output
causes.quote: Wind and solar output, which is generally low-priced, was low due to calm and cloudy weather conditions.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Heywood was flowing an average of 43 MW into South Australia during high prices, where its nominal capacity is 600 MW. This was a result of a constraint used to manage power system stability, limiting imports into South Australia and was forecast. At the same time, a constraint to manage the possible voltage collapse of the Bendigo to Kerang 220kV line in Victoria was forcing flows at an average of 27 MW out of South Australia across Murraylink.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding contributed to the high prices on 4 May (Attachment A - Significant rebids, 4 May) with between only 10 MW and 76 MW of high-priced capacity needed to meet demand.

causes.quote: Low temperatures in Queensland drove high demand... Demand for the 2 high-priced 5-minute intervals saw a demand increases of 81 and 178 MW from the preceding intervals and more expensive generation was needed to meet this increase.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: On-going base load outages in Queensland on the morning of 12 June were 1,850 MW.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: At 12.35 pm CS Energy's Kogan Creek unit tripped and removed 762 MW of capacity from the market. Then at 4.05 pm, InterGen's Millmerran unit 2 also tripped and removed a further 435 MW of capacity over two rebids.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: During the high-priced intervals, the Queensland to NSW interconnector (QNI) was importing 524 MW, which was around half its nominal capacity. This reduced limit was mostly due to a contingency constraint to avoid overloading Bayswater to Liddell power lines in NSW. Terranora, the other Queensland to NSW interconnector, was constrained by an outage of the Lismore static VAR compensator in NSW.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Wind generation was 127 and 139 MW during the high-priced intervals, out of a total of 831 MW of registered wind capacity in Queensland.

causes.label: solar_output
causes.quote: Given the time of day, there was little solar generation.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: With no available capacity for the 5.10 pm interval between $300 and $13,749 per MWh, the NEM dispatch engine found the cheapest NEM solution was to co-optimise between the energy and FCAS markets, resulting in the price of $11,639 per MWh.

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: Some generators were unable to ramp up generation fast enough. Some only started their plants after the 5.10 pm high price, and some were needed to provide FCAS. These factors resulted in some low-priced capacity unable to make it to market.
